Assess Orientation by asking date and place.
Asses Memory/registration by naming at least three objects [e.g. Ball, Table, Apple], then asking patient to repeat all three.
Assess language/receptive through three-stage command.
Assess language/repetitive by asking patient to repeat a sentence or phrase.
Assess language/naming by asking patient to name at least 2 common objects.

Position your hands approximately 1 to 3 feet from the patient's at the same eye level. Test visual fields (four quadrants for each eye by finger counting, each eye separately, or by detection of finger movement).
Observe direct pupillary responses to light in each eye.
Observe the indirect (consensual) papillary responses in each eye by ‘swinging flashlight’ test. Lights off.
Inspect patient’s eyes with ophthalmoscope at a height comfortable for you.
Test the cranial nerves III, IV, and VI by asking the patient to look right, up and down, and left, up and down in the shape of an 'H.'
Check for convergence.
Test cranial nerve VII motor function (upper division) by asking the patient raise eyebrows or squeeze eyes closed.
Test cranial nerve VII motor function (lower division) by asking the patient to show the teeth.

Test auditory acuity (cochlear nucleus of cranial nerve VIII) by whispering into each ear from two feet (or create a sound by rubbing your thumb and fingers together 10 cm from each ear, separately, and out of sight from the patient).
Observe the elevation of the palate (cranial nerve IX and X) with a tongue blade and light after instructing the patient to say “ah".
Test cranial nerve XI by asking the patient to rotate or turn his/her head against resistance.
Test cranial nerve XI by asking the patient to shrug the shoulders against resistance.
Test cranial nerve XII by asking the patient to stick out his/her tongue and move it from side to side as you observe.
Inspect muscle bulk of upper extremities.
Assess upper extremity distal tone: Extend and flex the wrist with patient relaxed (both sides).
Assess upper extremity proximal tone: Flex and extend the elbow with patient relaxed (both sides).
Test the deltoid muscle strength bilaterally.
Test the biceps muscle strength bilaterally.
Test the triceps muscle strength bilaterally.
Test wrist extension strength bilaterally.
Test fine finger movements through rapid tapping, bilaterally.
Pronator Drift Test: Ask the patient to close eyes and hold arms out in front of chest, palms facing ceiling. Observe for forearm pronation for at least 5 seconds.

Assess lower extremity proximal tone in both legs individually by flexing and extending the knee with patient in sitting position; or, if in supine position, by rapidly lifting behind knee allowing leg to flex passively.
Assess lower extremity distal tone by dorsiflexing and plantarflexing the ankles of both feet.
Test the hip flexor muscle strength on each side separately.

Test the knee extensor muscle strength bilaterally by asking the patient to push against your hand (placed on the ankle) or to maintain extended knee against resistance; then test knee flexor strength by asking patient to pull towards self.
Test distal strength by asking patient to dorsiflex the ankles against resistance.
Screen light touch sensation in both arms and both legs by a light brush (with tissue, cotton wisp, or fingers).
Demonstrate to the patient the difference between sharp and dull.
Describe first, then test cranial nerve V sensory function forehead (V1), cheek (V2) and jaw line (V3), with patient’s eyes closed.
Test sharp dull sensation on both arms (hands okay), with patient’s eyes closed.
Test sharp sensation on both legs (legs okay), with patient’s eyes closed.
Ask the patient to close eyes and then test vibration sense on each great toe with the $1 2 8 \mathsf { H z }$ tuning fork. Test vibratory sensation on lateral malleolus if not sensed on great toe.
Position sense: Ask the patient to close eyes while you slightly move the toe in an up or down direction.
Test the biceps reflex on each side.
Test the brachioradialis reflex on each side.
Test the triceps reflex on each side.
Test the patellar reflex on each side.
Test the Achilles reflex on each side.
Test the Plantar reflex on each side (for Babinski’s sign). ‘J’ or ‘L’ pattern toward big toe,
Test upper extremity coordination on each side with the finger-to-nose test.
Test for dysdiadokokinesia by having the patient alternately slap the front and back of hands against the thigh or other hand with increasing speed.
Test for lower extremity coordination on each side with the heel-to-knee-to-shin test.
Test for dorsal column signs with the Romberg Test.
Ask the patient to walk across the room, pivot and return while you observe the gait.
Ask the patient to walk away from you on tip toe and observe.
Ask the patient to walk toward you on heels and observe.
Ask the patient to walk heel-to-toe (tandem) and observe.
